proposed_title: Ittifaq l-ja2i7at dyal WHO: l-qawa3ed t9blat, walakin t-tatbi9 mazal fih as2ila
what_happened: On 20 May 2025, the World Health Assembly adopted the WHO Pandemic Agreement. This packet is a dated institutional explainer, not a claim about a new event on 7 September 2026: live retrieval was attempted on 2 September 2026 but the hosted search endpoint returned HTTP 401 and direct HTTPS requests were blocked by the Cloud proxy, so the status of later negotiations and ratifications is UNKNOWN.
key_facts: FACT — The World Health Assembly adopted the WHO Pandemic Agreement on 20 May 2025 after more than three years of negotiations triggered by inequities exposed during COVID-19.
FACT — WHO's adopted text addresses prevention, preparedness and response, including research, local production, technology transfer, supply chains and a coordinating financial mechanism.
FACT — Article 12 envisages a Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing system, but the adopted agreement says its operational annex must be negotiated separately.
FACT — The agreement does not give the WHO Secretariat power to order national lockdowns, vaccination mandates or changes to domestic law; states retain sovereign authority under the text.
UNKNOWN — The exact status on 7 September 2026 of the PABS annex, signatures, ratifications, entry into force, and Morocco's legal position could not be freshly retrieved and must not be inferred.

contradictory_evidence: Descriptions of the agreement as a completed global pandemic regime overstate the result because the PABS annex and domestic implementation remained separate work at adoption.
Claims that WHO acquired authority to impose national lockdowns or vaccine mandates conflict with the sovereignty clause and the institutional limits stated in the adopted text.
Calling adoption meaningless also goes too far: it creates agreed norms, but their practical force depends on subsequent consent, finance, annex negotiations and domestic action.
uncertainty: Medium. Adoption and the 2025 text are stable facts, but live retrieval failed. Every post-adoption milestone, including the position as of the future edition date, is UNKNOWN and needs a successful primary-source check before publication as current news.
context: COVID-19 exposed sharp gaps in access to vaccines, diagnostics and protective equipment. WHO members negotiated a new agreement alongside amendments to the International Health Regulations; these are distinct legal instruments and should not be conflated.
why_it_matters: Morocco is both exposed to cross-border health risks and interested in pharmaceutical capacity. The useful question is not whether a headline treaty exists, but whether benefit-sharing, financing and regional production become operational and equitable.
strategic_angle: Publish as a dated accountability card only. Explain what the adopted agreement does and does not do, then list the PABS annex, ratification, financing and Morocco position as questions requiring fresh verification.
